explanation: Francesco Baracca flew with a black prancing horse on his aircraft. In 1923 his mother suggested Enzo Ferrari use it for luck, and Ferrari set it on canary yellow, the colour of Modena.

claims.text: Ferrari's prancing-horse emblem comes from the horse painted on the aircraft of Francesco Baracca, an Italian fighter pilot of the First World War.
The emblems of Porsche, Lamborghini and Maserati did not come from Baracca's aircraft; Porsche's crest uses the horse of Stuttgart's coat of arms, Lamborghini's shows a bull and Maserati's a trident.
Francesco Baracca's aircraft carried a black prancing horse.
In 1923 Baracca's mother suggested that Enzo Ferrari use the prancing horse for good luck.
Ferrari set the horse on a canary-yellow background, the colour of the city of Modena.
